title: Annotatio III §.VI Decretum close: Continue the Leipzig collation; keep Christian moderation in teaching and writing; public prayers; Act Frankfurt 14 Sept. 1634 — stop before §.VII Cassellanum
pass_a_gloss: Besides these things certain proposals were made in best spirit by certain Legates: namely, that on one side they judged it advisable that the aforesaid Declaration (which concerns the mode of proceeding which the aforenamed Dury proposed, and the way of a colloquy of certain peaceable Theologians in which a unanimous confession of faith concerning the fundamental heads of our salvation can be instituted, after the example of that friendly collation which three years before was begun at Leipzig among Electoral Saxon, Brandenburg, and Hessian-Cassel Theologians) the upper Circles of the Empire should send at the first opportunity; and that by these Electors both foreign Princes and Kings should be invited by written Letters of Invitation: But on the other side Others also proposed this useful plan, that with each Elector’s, Prince’s, and Estate’s pretensions and rights saved, the Most Serene Electors Saxon and Brandenburg should be asked to deign to continue the friendly collation begun at Leipzig three years before, and to that end to appoint a convention at which other peaceable Theologians of either party summoned should also be present; and that in that convention regard should especially be had that consensus, so far as can be done, be modestly entered in a Christian and unanimous Confession which contains each and every head of Religion that concerns the foundation of salvation: but in the remaining heads scholastic dispute and contention is to be set aside. Besides these things also some openly declared their friendly consent in this: that meanwhile all Christian moderation and mildness is to be used by either party both in teaching and in writing; and to this end public prayers are to be framed in the temples of either party, by which the business may be commended to God Most High. In testimony of which matter this recess concerning this thing was made. Done at Frankfurt on the Main, 14 September, year 1634.
pass_b_english: Some legates also offered friendly proposals: that the Circles forward at once a declaration on Dury’s proposed procedure and on a peaceable theologians’ colloquy — modeled on the Leipzig collation three years earlier among Saxon, Brandenburg, and Hessian-Cassel electoral theologians — and that the Electors invite foreign princes and kings by letters.

Others usefully proposed that, saving each Elector’s, prince’s, and Estate’s rights, Electors Saxony and Brandenburg be asked to continue that Leipzig-friendly collation and call a convention where other peaceable theologians of either party can sit or send judgments — aiming at a modest Christian consensus-confession on every salvation-foundation head, while parking scholastic fights on the rest.

Several also agreed that meanwhile both sides should use Christian moderation and mildness in teaching and writing, and that public prayers for the work be framed in both parties’ churches, committing the business to God Most High.
This recess was made in witness of that. Done at Frankfurt am Main, 14 September 1634.
source_text: Adhaec quaedam optimo animo a Legatis quibusdam proposita fuere: nempe, quòd ab una parte consultum judicabant, ut praedictam Declarationem (quae de modo procedendi, quem praenominatus Duraeus proposuit, deque via, pacificorum quorundam Theologorum colloquium, in quo unanimis fidei de fundamentalibus salutis nostrae capitibus confessio institui possit, ad exemplum amicae illius collationis, quae ante triennium Lipziae inter Theologos Electorales Saxonicos, Brandenburgicos & Hassiacos-Cassellanos inita fuit) primo quoque tempore superiores Imperii Circuli mittant; atque ut ab hisce Electoribus invitentur scriptis Literis Invitoriis tam exteri Principes & Reges: Ab alia autem parte Alii hanc quoque proponebant utilem rationem, ut salvis cujusque Electoris, Principis & Status praetensionibus & juribus, rogarentur Serenissimi Electores Saxonicus atque Brandenburgicus, dignentur inceptam Lipziae ante tres annos amicam collationem continuare, atque hunc in finem conventum indicere, cui etiam alii utriusque partis evocati pacifici Theologi intersint; atque in eo conventu buc praesertim fore respiciendum, ut consensus, quoad fieri potest, modestè ineatur in Christiana atque unanimi Confessione, quae contineat omnia & singula, quae salutis fundamentum concernunt, Religionis capita: in reliquis autem capitibus disputationem atque contentionem Scholasticam esse seponendam. Praeter haec etiam & in hoc aliqui amicam consensionem suam apertè declararunt; quòd intereà temporis omnis ab utraque parte tàm in docendo, quàm scribendo Christiana moderatio & lenitas usurpanda sit; atque hoc fine, in utriusque partis templis, publicas preces esse concipiendas, quibus negotium Deo O. M. commendetur. In cujus rei testimonium hic recessus hac de re factus est. Actum Francofurti ad Moenum 14. Sept. Anno 1634.

rejected: to be buried as a corpse
